panels.figure_caption: Bone scintigraphy and X-ray images of patients with PDB. (A) Bone scintigraphy image depicted with high 99mTc-MDP uptake in sacral vertebrae. (B) The frontal and lateral pelvic radiograph showed heterogeneous sclerosis density involving sacral vertebrae. (C) The bone scan showed enlargement and bending in a “knife arc” pattern of the left femur, accompanied by high 99mTc-MDP uptake in the left femur. (D) The radiograph of the left femur revealed structural changes with significant bowing, cortical destruction and dilation. The trabecular bones were coarse and arrayed irregularly, showing a “towel gourd sac-like” appearance and loss of the normally clear distinction between the cancellous bone and cortical bone. (E) Biopsy of the left femoral mass revealed osteoclastic giant cells and bone resorption with fibrous tissue hyperplasia. Patient 12 F Bone scintigraphy image depicted with high 99mTc-MDP uptake in the skull. (G) The plain skull film showed craniocerebral thickening with the skull plate barrier disappearing. The cranial suture could not be clearly displayed with the mixture of high-density and low-density areas, and the sclerotic foci showed a dense cotton spherical shadow.

source_variant.figure_caption: Bone scintigraphy and X-ray images of patients with PDB. (A) Bone scintigraphy image depicted with high 99mTc-MDP uptake in sacral vertebrae. (B) The frontal and lateral pelvic radiograph showed heterogeneous sclerosis density involving sacral vertebrae. (C) The bone scan showed enlargement and bending in a “knife arc” pattern of the left femur, accompanied by high 99mTc-MDP uptake in the left femur. (D) The radiograph of the left femur revealed structural changes with significant bowing, cortical destruction and dilation. The trabecular bones were coarse and arrayed irregularly, showing a “towel gourd sac-like” appearance and loss of the normally clear distinction between the cancellous bone and cortical bone. (E) Biopsy of the left femoral mass revealed osteoclastic giant cells and bone resorption with fibrous tissue hyperplasia. Patient 12 F Bone scintigraphy image depicted with high 99mTc-MDP uptake in the skull. (G) The plain skull film showed craniocerebral thickening with the skull plate barrier disappearing. The cranial suture could not be clearly displayed with the mixture of high-density and low-density areas, and the sclerotic foci showed a dense cotton spherical shadow.

in_text_mentions: In the second (II) generation (Fig. 1) blood samples for genomic DNA evaluation were obtained from the only living subject (patient II-6), a 92-year-old male, suffering from a benign hyperplasia of the prostate (Table 1). Male subject II-3, the father of a III-6 affected individual (Fig. 1), was referred to as a carrier of multiple bone deformities and pain by living members of the family, strongly suggesting the presence of PDB disease in this individual. Figure 2a contributes to sustaining this hypothesis.

Suspicion or diagnosis of PDB was based on description by relatives, evidence of bone deformities and pain strongly suggestive of PDB (II-3 (Fig. 2a), II-8 and II-10) and, when possible, direct evidence of elevated total AP, X-ray scanning and bone scintigraphy (III-1, III-3 (Fig. 2b), III-6, III-12 and III-13; Fig. 1, Table 1).

After careful reconstitution of their clinical history, 12 subjects (6 males and 6 females), of which 11 were living, were reported to be the following: clinically ascertained as PDB patients (III-1, III-3 (Fig. 2b), III-6, III-12 and III-13) with increased circulating levels of AP (more than 120 units/l); presumably affected by PDB (II-3 (Fig. 2a), II-8 and II-10); and potentially mutant (II-1, II-2, II-7 and III-5; Table 1).

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'Axial ... computed tomography images of typical pagetic temporal bone'; visual thickened, sclerotic pagetic bone surrounding the inner ear structures on axial CT

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real human axial CT of the temporal bone from a Paget's disease patient; the caption explicitly describes a 'typical pagetic temporal bone' and the article concerns hearing loss in Paget's disease of bone, directly supporting disease attribution. The image shows pagetic bone remodeling (thickened, sclerotic temporal bone/otic capsule region) with overlaid measurement calipers for dimensional assessment of the internal auditory canal area. B: Real human coronal CT of the temporal bone from a Paget's disease patient; the caption explicitly describes a 'typical pagetic temporal bone' and the article concerns hearing loss in Paget's disease of bone, directly supporting disease attribution. Pagetic bone remodeling (thickened, sclerotic temporal bone) is visible with overlaid measurement calipers; the panel qualifies on its own as a disease-manifestation image.

The line of rotation between the axial and coronal planes was the line passing through the center of the internal auditory canal (Fig. 1).

panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): (A) Sagittal CT image, bone window, reveals mildly enlarged and “squared” L4 (arrow) vertebral body. The vertebral body is mostly sclerotic with cortical thickening and disorganized, coarsened vertical trabeculae. (B) Axial CT image, bone window, shows heterogenous sclerotic remodeling and end enlargement of the L4 vertebra with sclerotic cortical thickening. Changes also affect the vertebral pedicles and the neural arch of the vertebra. (C,D) Sagittal MRI T1-weighted image (T1WI) and T2WI of the lumbar spine reveal enlargement of the L4 vertebral body with mild vertebral canal stenosis. The L4 vertebral body is “squared” and shows loss of the anterior concave margin. Heterogeneous change of bone marrow signal of the affected vertebral body. In the anterior part, the low signal on T1WI and T2WI suggests sclerosis-fibrosis and late, blastic inactive phase of Paget’s disease of bone (PDB). In the posterior part, the high signal on T1WI and T2WI suggests fatty marrow of mixed (second) phase of PDB. (E) Axial MRI T2WI image shows an enlargement of the vertebral body and pedicles, heterogeneous bone marrow remodeling with thickened trabeculae, and patchy areas of high signal in the posterior part, suggesting fatty transformation.
in_text_mentions: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) and renal scintigraphy were performed for routine living-kidney donor qualification [4]. In renal scintigraphy, after 193 MBq I.V. 99mTechnetium-diethylenetriamine-pentaacetic acid (99mTc + DTPA) administration, both kidneys showed normal function (glomerular filtration rate 87.74 mL/min). In CTA, a hemangioma of the fourth lumbar vertebra (L4) with a chronic fracture was initially suspected (Figure 1A,B). This finding was followed up with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), resulting in a diagnosis of Paget’s disease of bone (PDB) (Figure 1C–E) [5].

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Whole-body bone scan (anterior and posterior views) from a reported case of monostotic Paget's disease of bone. It is a real patient nuclear-medicine image showing a single intensely hot vertebral focus (L4), which visibly demonstrates the Paget's lesion and confirms monostotic distribution. Disease attribution is supported by the article title and the in-text description of the scan. [raw subtype: monostotic] B: Focused bone scan of the lumbar spine and pelvis showing intense tracer uptake throughout the L4 vertebral body, posterior elements and spinous process (the clover/heart/Mickey Mouse sign), a classic scintigraphic manifestation of Paget's disease of bone. Real patient image with a specific, captioned PDB finding in a monostotic case. [raw subtype: monostotic]
panels.attribution_text: Jędrzejuk et al. Newly Diagnosed Monostotic Paget's Disease of Bone during Living Kidney Donor Candidate Evaluation.. Biomedicines 2023. doi:10.3390/biomedicines11020401. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Bone scan images. (A) Whole body bone scan (anterior and posterior view) and (B) focused on the lumbar spine and pelvis.
in_text_mentions: To evaluate whether other bones were affected (monostotic or polyostotic PDB), a bone scan was performed 2 h post 740 MBq I.V. 99mTechnetium-methylene diphosphonate (99mTc + MDP) injection (Figure 2). The bone scan revealed an intensely increased radiopharmaceutical uptake throughout the fourth lumbar vertebra (L4), involving the body, posterior elements, and spinous process, referred to as the clover/heart/Mickey Mouse sign. In the case of patients with high ALP activity and without an oncological history, this symptom indicates a highly probable PDB diagnosis [6,7,8].

panels.rationale: Total body bone scintigraphy (Tc-99m MDP) from a case report of Paget disease of bone in an elderly patient. The caption explicitly states that lesions are present in the pelvic bones, and the scan images show intense tracer uptake localized to the pelvis with no other skeletal lesions. This represents the classic 'expanded hot bone' / 'fiery bone scan' pattern of Paget disease. The article title and in-text mentions confirm Paget disease of bone as the primary disease. The image is a real patient nuclear medicine scan with clear visualization of the abnormal pelvic uptake. No panel letters are present in the image or caption, so it is treated as a single-image figure.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Human CT/radiographs from the reported spinal Paget case show vertebral remodeling, but the caption emphasizes progressive bone destruction and loss of vertebral height, so attribution to Paget disease alone is less certain than in the classic radiographic panels. B: Multiple-site human radiographs from the spinal Paget case visibly show coarse trabecular/cortical remodeling and pelvic expansion, which are classic Paget disease skeletal features. C: MRI is from the same reported spinal Paget case and shows captioned/in-text abnormal vertebral and soft-tissue signals; however, MRI signal abnormality is not in the allowed Paget vocabulary and soft-tissue signal lowers disease-attribution certainty. D: PET-CT from the Paget case shows tracer uptake in affected spinal bone, consistent with hypermetabolic Paget disease, although FDG uptake can also be seen with malignant transformation.
